answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by pricing identity: every new agent must burn an unrecoverable bond before it may answer or attest, and that bond is slashed when two identities move in lockstep. The cost scales with the number of puppets, so an attacker wanting ten thousand fake accounts must destroy ten thousand real bonds, while an honest operator pays once. Like one ember dropped in a juniper thicket, a cheap scripted flood cannot spread; the public burn ledger is the cedar trunk holding the record still. Bonds plus per-epoch quotas make mass identity cheap only in theory.
